title: Forgotten Realms Commander: card flavor text

paragraphs.text: Ride into legend.
Divine light forged in steel.
"Only victory shall stop our charge!"
Late at night, when dreams touch a studious mind, bouts of inspiration strike.
Each configuration reveals a potential future.
Get carried away.
Not alive, not dead, but definitely furious.
"Then we burn together!"
A fiery scourge for both flesh and soul.
Much more painful than mere regret.
Which burns more fiercely? Your ambition, or the flame?
From fuzzy to ferocious in an instant.
"Return to the earth and the wind."
The wilds consume, but they also create.
"I was raised on the stories of my ancestors, and I want to write my own pages in the tales."
No thought is as succulent as a secret.
No one returns unchanged.
The mountain will build your cairn of snow and ice and stone.
As long as it's never left empty, this magic pouch produces coins every dawn.
"Better the dead depart utterly than be enslaved."
"Zendikar will triumph this day, and our armies will fly with angels."
The aberrant magic of the Rimewind drew the unicorns back from the northern wastes to do battle once again.
"As this conflict grows, it gets harder to prevent the city from breaking down. How much longer can we keep this machinery balanced?"
A blazing sun that never sets.
There may exist powers even greater than Phyrexia.
The smallest seed of regret can bloom into redemption.
"Every choice alters the path of fate." —Sarkhan Vol
"I search for a vision of Zendikar that does not include the Eldrazi." —Expedition journal entry
"There shall be a vast shout and then a vaster silence." —Oracle *en*-Vec
The mizzium-sphere array drove her mind deep into the thought field, where only the rarest motes of genius may be plucked.
To consult a sphinx is a test in patience. Perhaps that's the point.
Idle chatter beckons many an attentive ear.
Only one vault was great enough to hold Emrakul.
Merfolk don't always know what they're looking for, but they're certain once they find it.
Even more than carrion, they crave the last words of the dying.
"The cost of your opposition will be extracted from your wits." —Nekusar, the Mindrazer
"Time flows as the rivers do, toward an unknown sea. The wise know to look downstream."
Serum was once derived from Mirrodin's blinkmoths, offering visions of inspiration. Now it is pulled from Phyrexian inkmoths, yielding visions of perfection.
Many necromancers share the same last words—the ones that conclude the undeath ritual.
When killing five just isn't enough.
It shambled from the cloud of ash and bone dust, undeterred by its own extinction.
"His tenement is filled with the most vile, disgusting vermin. It's infested with rats, too." —Branko One-Ear
"If it has ears, it will dance to my tune."
"My power is generosity, in a way. I give my survivors an appreciation for their lives."
"They may show up with the wrong thigh bone or mandible, but they always show up." —Zul Ashur, lich lord
All crave the Blessed Sleep. Few receive it.
"Die. But die knowing that your pathetic life will yield a great bounty for me." —Zul Ashur, lich lord
"Molten earth has no anger of its own. Only by infusing it with your own rage can the magma seethe and take shape." —Koth of the Hammer
"As I desire, so it shall be." —Nicol Bolas
"We train for the improbable, like lightning striking the same place twice, or striking everywhere at once." —Nundari, Sea Gate militia captain
Atarka conquered Qadat, the Fire Rim, long ago, winning over its efreet with a promise to spread the glory of fire to all the world.
Eyes are unnecessary for seeing the future.
A knight's devotion to their steed goes only so far.
Dinner and politics don't mix.
Atarka serving-goblins coat themselves with grease imbued with noxious herbs, hoping to discourage their ravenous masters from adding them to the meal.
"This world will be ruled by its rightful sovereigns, not these hideous pretenders."
Its wings shimmer with dreams absorbed from its enemies.
The storm rages and the earth breaks.
What was supposed to be a quiet time in town turned into an adventure of its own.
He collects the precious metals, and then converts the rest to propellant.
"Places, everyone!" —Judith
Those with knowledge are wise to listen to those with imagination.
"Where will you run when I punish you with the very ground you flee on?" —Nicol Bolas
The enormous can still be at the mercy of the small.
A dragon's scale can be carved into a mighty shield, provided you can procure a dragontooth to cut it.
The power of a waterfall. The fury of an avalanche. The intellect of a gale-force wind.
The forge of Purphoros burns in the heart of Mount Velus, attracting dragons with its blistering heat.
Attracting a dragon's attention may be the last mistake you make.
Beauty is in the eye of the exploder.
"Listen to the roar! Feel the thunder! The Immersturm shouts its approval with every bolt of lightning!"
It fears no sword and leaves no bones behind.
"Monsters dwell in every heart. We only think civilization tames them." ―Euphemia, Nexus watcher
"Might doesn't just build empires. It protects them." —Inti, Sun Empire knight
All seeds share a common bond, calling to each other across infinity.
An explorer's reward is a view of tomorrow's possibilities.
The true strength of nature is not the raging storm or the charging rhino, but the inexorable vitality of life.
"There's wisdom to be gained in death—whether it be one's own or someone else's." —Jarad, Golgari Lich-Lord
"Stay close, and their wrathful flames will not harm you." —Galea
Druidcraft is a simple invocation to spirits of nature, promising a glimpse of nature's secrets.
"There are many kinds of duty, and mine is to see our world grow and endure."
Nature grows solutions to its problems.
Hatred outlives the hateful.
"The curse is broken."
"Yes, nature is stronger. You don't see little buildings sprouting on trees." —Emmara
"Control the Great Conduit? You might as well try to divert a river with your hands."
First, whispers of ancient days. Then, visions of things to come.
If you stop to listen, you can hear it grow.
One offering to appease her on her arrival. Another to celebrate her departure.
"Her hunger knows no limit. Left unchecked, she would feast on all of Tarkir." —Yasova Dragonclaw
Its beak rends flesh and bone, exposing the tender marrow of dream.
Bant is a world where death and chaos hold no sway.
"It's easy to get taken in by the spectacle, to enjoy a bit of naughty amusement. But make no mistake: the Cult of Rakdos is a danger." —Tajic
Those who worship the great gargantuans could hardly be expected to fight with a subtle weapon.
All the aether charts in the world can't compete with the trained eye of a talented scout.
She follows the old tributaries built when merrows still shaped the tides.
Liliana whispered to whatever consciousness Oketra and Bontu had left. "You are the gods. He is the usurper. You know what to do."
Though Volrath is long dead, the slivers have become everything he wanted them to be: mindless instruments of destruction and despair.
No one is as dedicated to perfection as a stitcher working on their latest masterpiece.
All suns must set.
"I came seeking a challenge. All I found was you." —Zurgo, khan of the Mardu
Out of sight, into mind.
It started as a mere drop of water. The Magic Mirror crystallized it into much more.
Mirrodin's creator still lives, still shapes metal, and still commands world-shaking power.
During their endless travels, the mages of the Goma Fada caravan have learned ways to harness both life and death.
Forged by divine hands to wander mortal realms.
"There's only one way to be sure it's really dead."
"The heavens augur weal . . . for me. Woe for you."
"What do you have that I cannot obtain?" —Mairsil, the Pretender
Gruul territorial markings need not be legible. The blood, snot, and muck used to smear them are unmistakably Gruul.
"The crucible yields what you have forged in your mind. You need only reach in and draw the masterwork forth." —Wahara, Keeper of the Crucible
The impact sent the soldiers scattering—then something came out of the crater.
"What is mana but possibility, an idea not yet given form?" —Jhoira, master artificer
Made of bone and boiled in blood, a Rakdos signet is not considered finished until it has been used as a murder weapon.
Lost to time is the artificer's art of trapping light from a distant star in a ring of purest gold.
One who wears magical *boots of striding and springing* can jump astounding distances.
The blade glows only for Zendikar's chosen.
Its collapse is like the lashing out of a long-dead civilization that resents being forgotten.
Druids hold certain plants to be sacred and use their leaves and wood as a spellcasting focus.
"We must rely on our own knowledge, not on the dogma of the seekers or the mutterings of the sphinxes." —Tullus of Palandius
Bant's hearts are as pure as its air and as bright as its skies.
The continent of Murasa lies beneath a blanket of dense vegetation, its enormous branches tangled so thickly that some inhabitants never see the ground.
On the volcanic continent of Akoum, bizarre vegetation clusters around gas vents, and jagged mountain peaks rise high into the air.
"Approach my tower on bended knee or depart from it as ash upon the wind." —Gadwick, the Wizened
Underdark flooding has swallowed ancient drow burial chambers, which are now haunted . . . and infested with oozes.
Esper is an expansive canvas painted by precise, controlling hands.
"It was a strange morning. When we awoke, we found our trees transformed. We didn't know whether to water them or polish them." —Pulan, Bant orchardist
All are welcome.
If it can't be had here, it can't be had on any world.
Plant life in the valley changes for the worse as runoff from dwarven forges contaminates the water.
To find its center is to find one's own.
The continent of Ondu is a vast plateau crisscrossed by deep trenches and meandering rivers.
For wisdom's sake, it was built high to gaze on all things. For glory's sake, it was built high as a testament of power. For strength's sake, it was built high to repel all attacks.
Gnolls make offerings to sinister forces in the shadow-drenched chasms.
Legend says a mighty angel appears to pilgrims in need who reach this lofty height.
The continent of Guul Draz is a geothermal swampland reeking of heat and decay.
The ancient magic of sun elves keeps these lands in an eternal summer.
On the continent of Tazeem, rushing waters plunge through narrow canyons into mist-cloaked lakes.
Take two steps north into the unsettled future, south into the unquiet past, east into the present day, or west into the great unknown.
Far from human eyes, birds flit between vivid blossoms in a hidden paradise.
Wildflowers here bloom not with the season but with the ebb and flow of magic.
All the wonders of the natural world in one breathtaking microcosm.
Beauty appears in strange places for those with eyes to see it.
In the autumn, she casts her seeds across the streets below, and come spring, her children rise in service to the Conclave.
"The wind whispers, 'come home,' but I cannot." —Teferi
"We speak the dragons' language of flame and rage. They speak our language of fury and honor. Together we shall weave a tale of destruction without equal."
After lightning struck the cliffs, the ore became iron, the iron became steel, and the steel became greaves. The lightning never left.
